title: The redactor that leaked on failure
blurb: A detector error returned the original text unchanged.
prompt: During a detector outage, the redactor returned unredacted customer text with a warning header, and the audit topic contained sample values of the entities it removed. The model-generated draft fails open and logs removed values. Review it, fix it, and prove redaction fails closed and audits stay content-free.
aiNote: The draft catches detector errors and returns the original input with a degraded header, so an outage becomes a leak, and it publishes a sample of each removed value to the audit topic, putting the very data redaction exists to protect into a retained log.
testIdea: Stub the detector to fail and assert the response is a 503 with no text; run a redaction over an email address and assert the audit payload contains spans and counts but no address; request another tenant's document and assert 404.
followUps: When is regex fallback good enough, and when must redaction hard fail?
How would you verify redaction completeness without keeping the original?
What retention policy should span offsets have?
